problem: Zero-shot object navigation (ZSON) methods such as SP, SAVN and GMAN train only on seen objects with known labels. They ignore the seen-but-unlabeled objects in training scenes, so at test time agents confuse unseen targets with labeled seen objects and stop at the wrong one (e.g., stop at bread when told to find a knife).
motivation: Training scenes already contain many visually distinguishable objects whose labels are simply unused. Hiding the labels of some classes turns them into 'unknown' targets described only by attributes, which lets the agent practise navigating to unlabeled things before it meets truly unseen classes at test time. The authors also observe that unknown objects co-occur with known ones in specific contexts (a phone next to a laptop on a sofa), so relations between labeled and unlabeled objects can guide search.
key_idea: Split training classes into known (labeled) and unknown (label-hidden, attribute-described) targets, then learn meta-adapted labeled–unlabeled object relationships (LWMCM: attribute-to-image generation, an unlabeled-object detector, a contrastive feature modifier, and a self-supervised object graph) that feed an A3C LSTM policy.
insight: Most of the gain comes from simply training with unknown-object targets. In the Table IV ablation on AI2THOR, adding UOT alone lifts unseen SR/SPL from 18.50/8.05 to 28.00/21.88. TFG+UOI then give 31.40/22.07, MCFM gives 32.20/25.01, and the MOGL object graph gives 38.50/27.02, the largest single-module jump. Table V shows the MCFM contrastive loss and MCFM test-time meta-adaptation matter most: removing them gives unseen SR 35.30 and 36.40. Removing CCA-SSG or MOGL meta-updates costs little (37.80 and 38.30). There is a clear trade-off: known-object SR falls from 52.20 to 47.50 as unknown-object machinery is added and only partly recovers to 50.70 with MOGL. The authors call this negative transfer.
method: Unknown-object training split: object classes are divided into known C^k (labeled), unknown C^uk (present in training scenes but labels hidden; specified only by attributes such as 'Big, Ceramic, Receptacle') and unseen C^us (only in val/test scenes). The target indicator TI is a one-hot over the I known classes plus one 'unknown' slot, concatenated with an attribute embedding.

Target Feature Generator (TFG): an attribute-conditioned diffusion model, trained on known-object images and their attribute embeddings, runs ζ denoising steps to generate images for unknown/unseen classes. A frozen ImageNet ResNet-18 encodes these images into generative features g_t (d_g×512).

Unlabeled Object Identifier (UOI): position-embedded observation features f_o are concatenated with each unknown class's generative features and passed through 8 transformer layers. Outputs are averaged over the N classes, then a linear+ReLU layer gives f_t (256-d) and a linear head gives binary CLS ('an unlabeled object is in view'). It is pretrained with cross-entropy on unknown classes only, then frozen; the epoch with best identification rate (4th) is used.

Meta Contrastive Feature Modifier (MCFM): a TransE-style score S = ||f_k^c W1 + p W2 − f_t W3||² combines DETR known-object features (running-mean buffer per class) and 6-d egocentric coordinates (from DAT). A logistic loss pulls f_t toward known objects co-occurring in view and pushes it from absent ones. The output is f_t' = f_t + f_t W3, and the module is updated only when CLS=1.

Meta Object-Graph Learner (MOGL): a GCN F = ReLU(E·V·W^G) runs over (I+1) nodes (DETR known-object features plus f_t'). It is regularized by a CCA-SSG self-supervised loss between two randomly augmented graph views (η=1e-3).

Policy + meta-learning: FFN-projected f_o, graph output F and TI are concatenated with the previous action/state and fed to an LSTM, trained with A3C plus a 'done reminder' (from HOZ). MAML-style per-episode inner loops update MCFM (L_mcfm) and MOGL (L_cca) during both training and inference. The outer A3C loss updates MOGL and the rest. Training runs 6M episodes with 18 workers on 2×RTX 3090, all learning rates 1e-4.

setting.backbone: ResNet-18 (ImageNet, frozen) + DETR (frozen, trained on known objects) + attribute-conditioned diffusion generator (frozen) + transformer UOI (pretrained, frozen) + GCN/MCFM + LSTM A3C policy (trained from scratch with RL)
setting.training_data: A3C RL for 6M episodes in modified simulator scenes containing only known and unknown objects: AI2THOR 20 training rooms, RoboTHOR 60 training apartments. DETR and the diffusion TFG are pretrained on known objects (pre-collected images with attribute embeddings). UOI is pretrained on unknown-object classes. ResNet-18 is pretrained on ImageNet. No external web/LLM data.
setting.observation: egocentric RGB (ResNet-18 features + DETR detections with egocentric coordinates), plus target one-hot/unknown label and attribute embedding
setting.action_space: discrete: MoveAhead, RotateLeft, RotateRight, LookUp, LookDown, Done; success = Done within 1.5 m with target in view before step limit
setting.privileged: none for main method (test-time self-supervised meta-updates of MCFM/MOGL only); the 'Ours(GT)' variant replaces the UOI output CLS with ground-truth presence of unlabeled objects in view

numbers_note: All results are mean±std over 3 runs; only means are recorded. Metrics are reported separately for known, unknown and unseen object targets (keys suffixed _known/_unknown/_unseen); the unseen columns are the zero-shot results. Both benchmarks are the authors' own modified splits, not official challenge splits. GMAN is compared only on RoboTHOR, and its known-object SPL (16.80) is identical to SAVN's, which looks like a possible copy error. Ablations (Tables IV, V) are AI2THOR only. UOI identification success rate across pretraining epochs is shown only in a figure.
results: On AI2THOR, unseen-object navigation reaches SR 38.50 / SPL 27.02, versus the best baseline SP at 19.60 / 9.86 (+18.9 SR). Unknown-object navigation reaches 40.40 / 29.47, versus 20.80 / 10.11 for the best baseline values. On RoboTHOR, unseen objects reach 29.50 / 19.82, beating GMAN's 27.67 / 14.29 (+1.83 SR, +5.53 SPL), and unknown objects reach 31.20 / 20.10. Known-object performance is slightly below the plain DETR+LSTM baseline on both simulators (50.70 vs 52.20 and 40.20 vs 42.50 SR), which the authors call negative transfer.
limitations: Negative transfer: adding unknown objects lowers known-object SR/SPL relative to the baseline on both simulators.

Comparison fairness and scale: baselines (SP, SAVN, GMAN, Baseline) are trained without unknown-object targets, and evaluation uses custom small iTHOR/RoboTHOR splits (no GMAN comparison on AI2THOR, no official benchmark or real robot). The RoboTHOR unseen-object gain over GMAN is only +1.83 SR.
Performance collapses on long-range episodes (unseen SR 11.84 for L≥5) and on small objects. The imperfect UOI caps performance: the GT oracle adds about 3.7–3.9 SR on unknown/unseen targets.
